instruction: Write Node.js code that reads a text file asynchronously with fs/promises and logs its contents.
Write Node.js code that writes a JSON object to data.json with 2-space indentation using fs/promises.
Write Node.js code that reads and parses a JSON file, returning a default object when the file does not exist.
Write Node.js code that appends a timestamped line to app.log on each call.
Write Node.js code that recursively lists all .js files under a directory using fs/promises readdir with withFileTypes.
Write Node.js code that copies a file to a backup path and removes the original using fs/promises copyFile and unlink.
Write Node.js code that checks whether a path exists, is a file or a directory, using fs/promises stat and access.
Write a Node.js http server that responds with plain text "Hello, World!" on any path, listening on port 3000.
Write a Node.js http server implementing a tiny JSON API: GET /items returns an array, POST /items adds {id, name} to it.
Write Node.js code that performs an HTTP GET with the built-in https module and resolves the body as a string.
Write Node.js code that streams a large file to an HTTP response using createReadStream and pipe, with a Content-Type header.
Write Node.js code that reads a large file line by line using readline over a stream, counting lines without loading the file into memory.
Write Node.js code that deletes a file, tolerating the ENOENT case when the file is already missing.
Write Node.js code that creates a directory (and parents) then writes a file into it with fs/promises.
Write a Node.js http server that serves a static file safely, rejecting path traversal attempts outside the public directory.
Write Node.js code that buffers an incoming POST body, parses it as JSON and replies with 400 on invalid payloads.
Write Node.js code that watches a config file with fs.watch and reloads settings on change, tolerating the editor rename case.
Write a Node.js HTTP server with graceful shutdown: SIGTERM handler closes the server and finishes in-flight requests.
Write Node.js code that reads environment variables into a typed config object with validation, exiting on missing required variables.
Write Node.js code that pipes an HTTP request response directly to a file, downloading a URL with https and fs.
